newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 100 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 100 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 70 billion bolivar ($147 million) auction of 177-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 12.96 percent coupon.
The bank said it would also offer 15 billion bolivars ($32 million) in 267-day bills with a 13.17 percent coupon, and another 15 billion bolivars of 358-day bills with a 13.38 percent coupon.
Sixty billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday.

Coupons at the Wednesday auction are down from last week's 60 billion bolivar issue. Then 180-, 269- and 358-day notes carried 13.52, 13.74, and 13.97 percent coupons respectively for effective yields that softened as much as 55 basis points to historical lows of 12.97, 15.05 and 15.99 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
